objective: Determine whether auxiliary supervision of the intermediate destination-register values (steps 0 and 1) improves modular-addition generalization in the existing CyclicMGUPhase16Model and the learned representations supplied to the fixed cyclic ALU.
hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS (not a proven cause): terminal-only supervision may allow the learned read/write/gate pathways to fit the final answer without learning intermediate representations compatible with the ALU's canonical harmonic coordinate system. This experiment tests whether intermediate destination-value supervision helps.
scientific_distinction: The cyclic ALU is fixed and analytical. Any improvement from this intervention concerns the supervision of the learned read, write and gate networks around it; it is not evidence of learned arithmetic from data.

target_definition.verification: matched Phase16RegisterTask.simulate_trace() on every allowed example

metric_definitions.c_read: mean of the per-role mean cosine(u_a, Phi(a)) and cosine(u_b, Phi(b)) at step 2
metric_definitions.s_context: unweighted mean over digits of the mean pairwise cosine similarity of same-integer step-2 operand reads pooled across role and context
metric_definitions.c_alu: mean cosine of the raw cyclic_alu(u_a, u_b) tensor at step 2 with Phi((a+b)%10)
metric_definitions.c_dest: mean of the step-0/1/2 mean cosines of u_dest_post with Phi(y_destination_t)
metric_definitions.cosine_guard: denominator epsilon 1e-08; similarity 0.0 if either norm < 1e-07
